transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-09
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Ethan (Redwood SA), Dr. Maria Gomez, Liam P., Sandra O., Noah R., Kelsey T.

Summary:
Quick kickoff to align on POC timeline, success criteria (latency/accuracy/security), access gating, and benchmarking plan. Agreed on key milestones: kickoff (today), access & pre-provisioning (by 12/16), mid-point review (1/6), exec readout (week of 1/24).

Topics:
- Success criteria (latency p95, throughput qps, quality thresholds for clinical extraction)
- Workload sizing and dataset needs
- Benchmark definitions and scripts (latency, TPU/GPU sizing, token-cost tracking)
- Access steps: VPC peering/IP allowlist, SSO, KMS details
- Timeline & checkpoints, roles and owners

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we're excited to kick this off with Elysian. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Maria: Maria here, hi.
[00:10] Liam: Liam, ML eng.
[00:12] Sandra: Sandra, regulatory.
[00:15] Noah: Noah, infra.
[00:18] Kelsey: Kelsey, product.
[00:20] Jordan: Great. Priya, Ethan from our side as well. So agenda — align on success criteria, access gates, bench plan and timeline.
[00:30] Priya: Cool. I'll start with the bench definitions cause that tends to drive the size and the infra ask. For us a typical POC bench has three parts: correctness/quality (the domain specific metrics you care about), latency targets measured p50/p95, and throughput under sustained load. For medtech use cases we usually include an extraction accuracy threshold plus hallucination rate check.
[00:55] Liam: For our internal bar, we need entity extraction F1 > 0.82 on the anonymized clinical notes and hallucination below 3% on the test set. Latency needs to be under 150 ms p95 for single-shot inference on the short prompts; batch jobs (bulk extraction) can be slower.
[01:15] Priya: Okay F1 .82 and hallucination <3% noted. For latency p95 150ms, we should validate on the same sequence lengths you expect — you mentioned short prompts, what's the token distribution?
[01:28] Liam: Most prompts are 40 to 120 tokens, average about 65. Bulk extraction runs 10k documents overnight, but realtime UX is the 40–120 token path.
[01:40] Ethan: Good to know. That means we will pick model variants that match that length profile — we can try both a quantized 8-bit-ish variant and a float16 variant on our Dedicated pool to compare cost/latency.
[01:55] Maria: Are we assuming Hosted or Dedicated?
[01:58] Jordan: Good q. We recommend starting on Redwood Hosted to get rapid time-to-results, but because you have PHI and regulatory constraints Sandra, we discussed Private (VPC) as an option. For the POC we can do a dedicated private lane — Redwood Private with customer-managed VPC peering so no data leaves your VPC, and we can enable KMS integration.
[02:20] Sandra: Right, PHI is non-negotiable. We need SOC 2 and ISO references, full audit logs and KMS/HSM integration. Also SSO (SAML) for the console.
[02:32] Priya: We'll attach our SOC 2 and ISO artifacts, and the audit-log export format. SSO config is straightforward, we'll send the SAML metadata. For KMS, we support either AWS KMS or customer HSM; we'll need a key alias and policy.
[02:47] Noah: From infra side — we prefer peered VPC and static egress IPs for allowlisting, please provide the IP ranges. Also any agent or connector?
[02:58] Jordan: There are two patterns: 1) peered VPC with private link, or 2) managed connector that uses egress IPs — we'll send the preferred flow and sample CloudFormation.
[03:10] Kelsey: Timeline? We need to align this with Q1 board readout so the exec readout date is important.
[03:16] Jordan: Proposed timeline — today kickoff; Redwood to send access checklist by 12/11; customer to provision staging VPC, open IP ranges, create service account by 12/16; Redwood to provision POC environment and share endpoints by 12/20; run bench sprint 12/21–01/03 (holidays aware); mid-point review 2027-01-06; buffer week then exec readout tentatively 2027-01-27. Does that sequence fit?
[03:42] Maria: Looks fine but can we compress some dates? 12/20 provisioning is tight for us.
[03:48] Jordan: We can aim to have endpoints earlier if infra is ready — Priya, what's minimum lead time?
[03:53] Priya: If Noah's team can share access + allowlist by 12/14, we can stand up a staging fleet by 12/17. So we pushed the critical owner work to Noah and Liam for data.
[04:05] Noah: Ok 12/14 we can have allowlist and a service account, depends on internal change window but likely doable.
[04:12] Liam: I'll get anonymized samples to you. Can you confirm what size and format you need?
[04:17] Priya: CSV with prompt plus expected json output is ideal, around 2GB sample ideally but we can start with smaller. We'll attach a sample template.
[04:25] Jordan: Benchmark details — Priya, walk through the metrics we'll run.
[04:28] Priya: Sure. We'll run: 1) single-query latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) for your three canonical prompts; 2) throughput sweep to measure qps at target latency bands; 3) cost per thousand tokens using our token accounting; 4) QA harness to compute extraction F1 and hallucination. We'll run each bench across two model configs: a higher-accuracy float16 and a quantized lower-cost config. Results will be posted to the shared spreadsheet.
[04:56] Liam: For throughput, our ramp target is 50 qps sustained for the realtime flow.
[05:00] Priya: Noted 50 qps. For sizing that'll drive number of GPUs in the dedicated pool. We'll include recommended pool sizing and autoscaling triggers in the report.
[05:10] Maria: How will you measure hallucination? It's a bit fuzzy.
[05:13] Priya: We'll use a combination of exact-match checks for entity values and heuristic checks flagged as potential hallucinations. We'll surface flagged cases for manual review; the F1 is computed on agreed labeled set. If you want, we can add an extra 'safety pass' with a reranker.
[05:29] Sandra: Also need to show logs and retention. For compliance we need 1-year retention of audit trails and the ability to export logs.
[05:36] Ethan: We have configurable retention; for POC we can enable exports to your S3 bucket or to a syslog endpoint. We'll note the retention config in the access guide.
[05:45] Noah: Network policy — any special ports?
[05:48] Priya: Only standard HTTPS 443, plus our health check ports if you use peering; we'll list them.
[05:53] Jordan: Okay let's confirm success criteria so we can lock the POC gates: (1) Quality: entity extraction F1 >= 0.82 on the canonical set; hallucination <= 3%; (2) Performance: p95 latency <= 150ms for 40–120 token prompts and support 50 qps sustained without >10% error rate; (3) Security/compliance: Private deployment with KMS and audit logs enabled and SOC2 artifacts provided; (4) Ops: ability to run automated bench scripts and produce reproducible results.
[06:25] Maria: That list looks good. We'll add an internal requirement that the model does not persist PHI in logs — is that guaranteed?
[06:33] Priya: We can configure to avoid storing request/response payloads in logging; for PII/PHI we recommend redaction in your preprocessor and we can enable no-payload logs and only keep metadata. We'll document exactly what is stored.
[06:46] Liam: For the POC, do you recommend we test 2 model sizes?
[06:50] Priya: Yes: float16 base and an 8-bit quantized variant. That gives a clear comparison on perf vs cost.
[06:56] Kelsey: On reporting — will you provide a slide deck / exec summary?
[06:59] Jordan: Yes we'll prepare an exec readout slide deck summarizing results and recommendations, and a detailed bench spreadsheet that includes raw numbers and the scripts.
[07:09] Maria: Any blockers from Redwood side?
[07:12] Priya: None, but we need the sample dataset, allowlisting, and SAML metadata.
[07:18] Noah: We'll try to get those in by 12/14.
[07:21] Jordan: Great. Quick risk callouts: holiday window might reduce bench time; we'll run a condensed bench if needed and extend the mid-point window if raw results need more time. Also note model fallbacks — if Dedicated pool saturated we'll fallback to a compatible hosted variant but since this is private peered, fallback is limited. We'll discuss fallback policy in the runbook.
[07:46] Sandra: On legal, procurement will need our security addendum; can you send standard terms and the specific SOC/ISO docs?
[07:54] Jordan: Yes, I'll send the legal packet and SOC artifacts.
[07:57] Kelsey: Ok next steps recap?
[08:00] Jordan: I'll recap: Redwood sends access checklist + SAML + SOC docs by 12/11; Priya sends bench scripts + sample template by 12/15; Elysian shares anonymized sample + open IP ranges by 12/14; Redwood stands up staging endpoints by 12/17; bench run 12/21–01/03; mid-point 01/06; exec readout week of 01/24 (tentative 01/27).
[08:29] Maria: Sounds good. Thanks all.
[08:31] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.
